the development and application of improved methods for discriminated and quantifying PBAPs.
the development of new methods to discriminate and quantify primary biological aerosol using fluorescence data from the WIBS instrument.

the methods presented here provide the best possible approach to cluster fluorescent particle data, and should be applied in all cases.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the methods used here are able to discriminate and quantify primary biological aerosol with a higher degree of certainty than previous methods.

the Ward linkage, z-score or range data normalisation method can be employed to cluster WIBS data, with the Ward linkage with range normalisation being the preferred method due to its computational efficiency.
the z-score method is better at identifying and quantifying bacterial aerosol and the range method is better at detecting and quantifying fungal spores.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the methods we present here allow for the explicit attribution of each particle in a data-set to clusters, reducing the potential for mis-assignment of particles and improving the quality of cluster definition and discrimination.

the use of explicit cluster assignment for each particle in a data-set is superior to comparative attribution methods that use subsampling and that hierarchical agglomerative clustering methods with z-score or normalisation by range perform best.
it provides a new tool for the analysis of fluorescent particle data from WIBS instruments that is more accurate and robust than previous approaches.
